name: Turkmenistan
headline: Turkmenistan: +3.6% growth in 2025, 2.7% inflation, debt 3% of GDP
sections: Turkmenistan is a $77.4 billion economy (2025), the world's 89th-largest of 215 measured. Real output grew +3.6% in 2025, close to the world median of +3.5%. Income per person is $23K at purchasing-power parity (2025), against a world median of $21K.

Consumer prices rose 2.7% in 2025, broadly within typical target ranges, down from 11.2% in 2022. Unemployment stood at 4.3% (2025), below the world median of 5.1%. Youth unemployment was 10.0% (2025).
Gross government debt is 3% of GDP (2025), a low level that has fallen from 15% in 2020. The general government balance is +0.1% of GDP (2025), a surplus.
The current account balance is +1.7% of GDP (2025). Trade equals 28% of GDP (2025), a relatively closed economy. Net FDI inflows were 1.4% of GDP (2025).
IMF projections put government debt at 3% of GDP by 2031, broadly stable from today's level. Life expectancy is 70.2 years (2024). Population: 6.7 million (2025).
note: Built from official World Bank and IMF data; IMF projections are labelled as projections.
